ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $OP$ bisects $\angle AOB$, $E$ is a point on $OA$, $OE=4$, and the distance from $P$ to $OB$ is 2. What is the area of $\triangle OPE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw PD$\perp$OB at point D and PC$\perp$OA at C, \\
since $OP$ is the bisector of $\angle AOB$, and the distance from P to OB is 2, \\
therefore $PC=PD=2$, \\
since $OE=4$, \\
therefore the area of $\triangle OPE$ is $\frac{1}{2}OE\cdot PC=\frac{1}{2}\times 4\times 2=\boxed{4}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, point O is on the left side, OA is the horizontal side from O to the right, and A is marked at the right end; OB is the side slanting from O to the upper right, and B is marked above; OP is located between OA and OB and passes through point P, indicating the internal angle bisector of angle AOB; point E is located on the horizontal side OA, and the line segment EP together with OP and OE forms triangle OPE. Then reason: because OE is on OA, when finding the area of triangle OPE, OE can be taken as the base. Draw a perpendicular from P to OA, and its length is the height with OE as the base. It is known that OP bisects angle AOB, and a point on the angle bisector has equal perpendicular distances to the two sides of the angle; it is also known that the distance from P to OB is 2, so the distance from P to OA is also 2. Therefore the area of triangle OPE is (1/2)×OE×height = (1/2)×4×2 = 4.
